units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Coldly .
I never take supper, thank you, Vicomte.
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: The VICOMTE is about to retire .
LADY BASILDON, seeing this , rises at once and takes his arm .
But I will come down with you with pleasure.
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: I am so fond of eating! I am very English in all my tastes.
units.name: VICOMTE DE NANJAC

units.text: You look quite English, Vicomte, quite English.
units.name: LADY BASILDON

units.text: They pass out .
MR. MONTFORD, a perfectly groomed young dandy , approaches MRS. MARCHMONT.
Like some supper, Mrs. Marchmont?
units.name: MR. MONTFORD

units.text: Languidly .
Thank you, Mr. Montford, I never touch supper.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: Rises hastily and takes his arm .
But I will sit beside you, and watch you.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: I don’t know that I like being watched when I am eating!
units.name: MR. MONTFORD

units.text: Then I will watch some one else.
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: I don’t know that I should like that either.
units.name: MR. MONTFORD

units.text: Severely .
Pray, Mr. Montford, do not make these painful scenes of jealousy in public!
units.name: MRS. MARCHMONT

units.text: They go downstairs with the other guests , passing SIR ROBERT CHILTERN and MRS. CHEVELEY, who now enter .
And are you going to any of our country houses before you leave England, Mrs. Cheveley?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Oh, no! I can’t stand your English house-parties. In England people actually try to be brilliant at breakfast. That is so dreadful of them! Only dull people are brilliant at breakfast. And then the family skeleton is always reading family prayers. My stay in England really depends on you, Sir Robert.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Sits down on the sofa .
Taking a seat beside her .
Seriously?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Quite seriously. I want to talk to you about a great political and financial scheme, about this Argentine Canal Company, in fact.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: What a tedious, practical subject for you to talk about, Mrs. Cheveley!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Oh, I like tedious, practical subjects. What I don’t like are tedious, practical people. There is a wide difference. Besides, you are interested, I know, in International Canal schemes. You were Lord Radley’s secretary, weren’t you, when the Government bought the Suez Canal shares?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Yes. But the Suez Canal was a very great and splendid undertaking. It gave us our direct route to India. It had imperial value. It was necessary that we should have control. This Argentine scheme is a commonplace Stock Exchange swindle.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: A speculation, Sir Robert! A brilliant, daring speculation.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Believe me, Mrs. Cheveley, it is a swindle. Let us call things by their proper names. It makes matters simpler. We have all the information about it at the Foreign Office. In fact, I sent out a special Commission to inquire into the matter privately, and they report that the works are hardly begun, and as for the money already subscribed, no one seems to know what has become of it. The whole thing is a second Panama, and with not a quarter of the chance of success that miserable affair ever had. I hope you have not invested in it. I am sure you are far too clever to have done that.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: I have invested very largely in it.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Who could have advised you to do such a foolish thing?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Your old friend—and mine.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Who?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Baron Arnheim.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Frowning .
Ah! yes. I remember hearing, at the time of his death, that he had been mixed up in the whole affair.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: It was his last romance. His last but one, to do him justice.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Rising .
But you have not seen my Corots yet. They are in the music-room. Corots seem to go with music, don’t they? May I show them to you?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Shaking her head .
I am not in a mood to-night for silver twilights, or rose-pink dawns. I want to talk business.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Motions to him with her fan to sit down again beside her .

I fear I have no advice to give you, Mrs. Cheveley, except to interest yourself in something less dangerous. The success of the Canal depends, of course, on the attitude of England, and I am going to lay the report of the Commissioners before the House to-morrow night.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: That you must not do. In your own interests, Sir Robert, to say nothing of mine, you must not do that.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Looking at her in wonder .
